title: Map Reading and Interpretation
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use a Survey of Kenya topographical sheet if the school has one. Area: count full squares, then half squares as halves.

skills.key_step: The child reads marginal information, calculates areas by squares and names the ways relief is shown.

floor.prerequisite: Describes Africa's features and uses latitude and longitude.
floor.question: Which line is 0 degrees latitude?

steps: Read the margin: title, scale, key, north, sheet number.
contexts: a survey map of a county
a lake shown over grid squares

board.do: Draw a 4 by 3 grid with a lake covering it.

board.say: How many squares does the lake cover?

misconceptions.ask: What does the key (legend) of a map show?
misconceptions.repair: Look at the key of a real map.

misconceptions.ask: A lake covers 4 grid squares by 3 grid squares of 1 square kilometre each. What is its area?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the squares and count them.

misconceptions.ask: Which shows relief on a topographical map?
misconceptions.repair: Look at a real map for the lines that join heights.

misconceptions.ask: A brown curved line on a topographical map joins points of the same height. What is it?
misconceptions.repair: Check the key: contours are brown lines labelled with heights.

checks.question: A lake covers 5 by 2 grid squares of 1 square km each. What is its area?
Give one way relief is shown on a topographical map.
checks.answer: any of: contours, spot heights, trigonometrical stations, hill shading, layer colouring
